Convert a submodel fit of class projpred_mlvl to class glmerMod

Source: R/mlvl_laplace.R
as_glmerMod.Rd

For binomial and Poisson multilevel submodels with random intercepts, projpred uses its own fit, which has class projpred_mlvl (see section "Draw-wise divergence minimizers" of projpred-package). This function builds the corresponding lme4 object, for use with the methods of lme4. It does not fit the submodel again: it evaluates the objective of lme4::glmer() (with nAGQ = 1) once, at the parameter estimates of object.

Usage

as_glmerMod(object, data, weights = NULL)

Arguments

object

An object of class projpred_mlvl, for example an element of element outdmin of an object returned by project().

data

A data.frame with the data that object was fitted to: the predictors, the grouping variables and the response, with the names used in formula(object). The object does not store these data. In the traditional projection, the response of a submodel fit is the vector of the reference model's predicted means (success probabilities for the binomial family) for the projected draw or cluster. In the augmented-data projection, the data are the augmented rows (one row per observation and response category), and the predicted probabilities are in the weights.

weights

A numeric vector of the observation weights that object was fitted with, or NULL for weights of 1. Rows of data with weight 0 are removed, as projpred does before it fits a multilevel submodel.

Value

An object of class glmerMod (see lme4::glmer()) with the fixed effects, the group-level standard deviations and the group-level intercepts of object.

Details

The group-level intercepts of the returned object are computed by lme4 from data and weights. If they or the value of the objective function at the parameter estimates differ from those of object, then data or weights are not those of the fit, and this function throws a warning.

For non-integer responses, lme4 versions up to 2.1-0 round binomial responses in the log-likelihood and give a log-likelihood of -Inf for the Poisson family. With these versions, the log-likelihood of the returned object (and what depends on it, for example AIC()) is not that of the fit; the parameter estimates and the predictions are not affected.

The call stored in the returned object is the lme4::glmer() call for data and weights, with the default settings of lme4::glmer().

Examples

# Data:
set.seed(1)
dat <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(120), x2 = rnorm(120),
                  g = factor(rep(1:8, each = 15)))
dat$y <- rbinom(120, 1, plogis(0.8 * dat$x1 + rnorm(8)[dat$g]))

# The `stanreg` fit which will be used as the reference model (with small
# values for `chains` and `iter`, but only for technical reasons in this
# example; this is not recommended in general):
fit <- rstanarm::stan_glmer(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + (1 | g), family = binomial(), data = dat,
  chains = 2, iter = 500, refresh = 0, seed = 9876
)
#> Warning: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess
#> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess

# Projection onto a multilevel submodel, with a single cluster (so the
# response of the submodel fit is the mean of the reference model's
# predicted success probabilities over the posterior draws):
refm <- suppressWarnings(get_refmodel(fit))
prj <- project(refm, predictor_terms = c("x1", "(1 | g)"), nclusters = 1)
fit_sub <- prj$outdmin[[1]]

# Conversion (the name of the response is taken from the formula of the
# submodel fit):
dat_sub <- dat
dat_sub[[all.vars(formula(fit_sub))[1]]] <- rowMeans(refm$mu)
fit_lme4 <- as_glmerMod(fit_sub, data = dat_sub, weights = refm$wobs)
lme4::ranef(fit_lme4)
#> $g
#>   (Intercept)
#> 1  0.20921382
#> 2  0.67702021
#> 3  0.08850761
#> 4 -0.02651275
#> 5  0.45002772
#> 6 -0.49389935
#> 7 -0.26729176
#> 8 -0.59042784
#> 
#> with conditional variances for “g”
